question.problem:
Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.

${\int }_{3}^{9}\frac{4{log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2})}{x}\,\text{d}x=($
{{field-1}}
$)\operatorname{ln}⁡3$
question.worked_solution:
Let $u={log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2}).$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\cdot 2x=\frac{2}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\,⟹\,\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{2}\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $3$ | $9$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $2$ | $4$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{3}^{9}\frac{4{log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2})}{x}\,\text{d}x & =4{\int }_{3}^{9}{log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2})\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =4{\int }_{2}^{4}u\cdot \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡3{\int }_{2}^{4}u\,\text{d}u \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡3\cdot \frac{{u}^{2}}{2}{|}_{2}^{4} \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡3(16-4) \\  & =(12)\operatorname{ln}⁡3\end{aligned}
$$
